title: PinkRoccade serves the ideal verticals but its own-product model disqualifies it
content:
PinkRoccade's healthcare and local-government units cover the two verticals the thesis targets most directly — the assessment calls them ideal — and the row is still filed do-not-pitch. The reason recorded is the model: it sells its own vertical products rather than assembling and integrating other people's components.

That inversion is the point worth keeping. Vertical fit describes where a firm's customers are; the delivery model describes whether a new layer can be introduced at all. A product vendor's answer to a missing audit trail is a roadmap item in its own software, and its customers buy an application, not an architecture they own. There is no seam for a third-party record layer to attach to, and any capability added there competes with the vendor's own release plan.

The record also carries a data-quality warning: the figures held for PinkRoccade are fifteen years old. Nothing size- or growth-dependent in the assessment can be trusted, and only the structural finding — product-led, in the right verticals — survives that staleness.
